newsitem.title: INDIA: Paribas downgrades India Mahindra GDRs.
newsitem.headline: Paribas downgrades India Mahindra GDRs.

text.p: Paribas Capital Markets said it was downgrading the global depositary receipts (GDRs) of Indian automobile firm Mahindra & Mahindra to "no action" from "buy."
"This follows the recent outperformance of the GDR relative to all the GDRs in the GDR universe, and relative to the Indian market," Paribas analyst Rajeev Das said in a report.

"While we are still positive on the longer term prospects of the company, we think that the GDR's outperformance precludes more outperformance in the near future, especially now that TELCO and Bajaj Auto GDRs seem attractive in comparison to Mahindra," the report said.
It said part of the reason the Mahindra shares outperformed the market in recent times was that the stock had lagged the sector's growth in the last few years.
Following the company's first half results, the GDRs may actually underperform the sector and the market as fund managers try to book profits, the report said.
"Investors may even consider selling ahead of the market and perhaps buy on declines," it said. "Our no action recommendation stems from our longer-term view of the stock vis-a-vis the market."
